stops.note: origin disputed, perhaps from séibe 'mug, measure'; these unlicensed drinking dens often sold untaxed poitín
carried abroad by Irish emigrants; in South Africa, township shebeens such as those of Soweto served Black drinkers barred from licensed bars until the liquor laws changed in 1961-62

current_meaning: an unlicensed bar, especially in Ireland, Scotland or South Africa
